The paper considers the Skorokhod embedding problem, in particular the Root solution in the formulation of Loynes.
Root's solution minimizes the expected residual of the stopping time τ, which is important for finding no-arbitrage lower bounds for VIX call options.

The paper assumes the underlying process X is a continuous Markov process with continuous marginal densities and the target measure μ has no atoms and its absolutely continuous part is locally bounded away from zero.
A discontinuity in the barrier function leads to thin and thinner corridors, causing the density of the target measure μ to vanish at the end of the corridors approaching the discontinuity.
The main result is that if the target measure μ has no atoms and its absolutely continuous part is locally bounded away from zero, then the barrier function r is continuous and finite.
The paper provides lemmata that formalize the heuristics of how a discontinuity in the barrier function affects the target measure.

The paper concludes with an example that resembles the situation of a discontinuous barrier function, showing that conditions on the density of the target measure are indeed needed to ensure continuity of the barrier function.
The paper assumes the underlying process X is a continuous Markov process, but the main results only require the process to be continuous with continuous marginal densities.
The paper uses the regularity of the barrier function r, which ensures uniqueness of the existing barrier function.
The paper mentions that most progress related to Root's solution has been made in generalizing existence results instead of regularity results.
